test_title: PYST 42: SSC MTS 2024 - Numerical and Mathematical Ability (Held On: 30 Oct, 2024 - Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: The diameter of a hollow hemisphere is 40 cm. Water is filled in it up to its brim. When spherical lead shots each of diameter 0.8 cm are dropped into the hemisphere, three-fifths of the water flows out. How many lead shots were dropped into the hemisphere?
solution:
**Given:**

Diameter of hollow hemisphere = 40 cm ⇒ Radius (R) = 20 cm

Diameter of 1 lead shot = 0.8 cm ⇒ Radius (r) = 0.4 cm

Water overflow = 3/5 of hemisphere volume

**Formula used:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2)/(3) pi R³

Volume of sphere = (4)/(3) pi r³

Number of lead shots = Volume of water overflow ÷ Volume of 1 shot

**Calculations:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × 20³ = (2/3) × π × 8000 = 16000π/3

Water overflow = (3/5) × 16000π/3 = 3200π

Volume of 1 lead shot = (4/3) × π × 0.4³ = (4/3) × π × 0.064 

Number of lead shots = 3200π ÷ [(4/3) × π × 0.064] = 37500

**∴ Number of lead shots = 37500**
